channel.title: St Helen's Sunday talks podcast
channel.description: One thing matters; taking the time to listen to Jesus. Every week we gather together on Sundays to hear God speak through the Bible. This podcast is a feed of our three English speaking talks from our Sunday services. We are a church based in the heart of the City of London. Visit www.st-helens.org.uk or download our apps on iOS and Android, to access thousands of talks and other resources.

item.title: The divine king
item.description: George Diwakar - At Christmas we sing about 'the little Lord Jesus', but Psalm 110 shows us a far bigger Lord Jesus. In this psalm David hears the LORD speak to the one David calls 'my Lord', who is seated on God’s own throne, rules over God’s defeated enemies and gathers people who gladly serve him. We look at what this psalm shows us about King Jesus, and why it should make us want to offer ourselves freely to his service.

item.title: God’s certain promise
item.description: Nick Heeley - The world hopes things will get better, but often it’s just wishful thinking. In Genesis 15, God the creator gives Abram certainty of a future family, who will dwell in a future home. As Christians, these promises are ours, as we share the faith of Abram. We trust the same promises, and can be certain of a future home with our Lord God.

item.title: Salvation from death and sin
item.description: Jack Stileman - One day you will die. Most of us avoid thinking about it because it’s terrifying. And most of us carry a penny-sized impression of Jesus: a spiritual teacher, a religious leader, someone to take or leave. Someone who can’t help us here. But in Luke 8:40-56, a desperate father and a bleeding woman discover how small that view is. Jesus is the unprecedented Saviour who rescues us from death and sin. So do not fear; only believe.

item.title: Salvation from the devil
item.description: Jack Stileman - On the far side of the lake, Jesus meets a man whose life has been torn apart. He lives among the tombs, cut off from his town and controlled by a host of demons. Luke shows us plainly that the devil’s work is to destroy. Yet with a single word Jesus sets the man free, and we find him clothed, in his right mind and sitting at Jesus’ feet. Who do you want to be Lord of your life?

item.title: The Son is the light of the world
item.description: William Taylor - One of the most disturbing features of the teaching of Jesus is the way that it exposes us in our human limitations and failures. Jesus’ claim to be the light of the world suggests that he, and he alone, can provide true enlightenment. At the same time, it implies that any who refuse to recognise him remain – in the dark.

item.title: Salvation from disorder
item.description: George Diwakar - In a broken world filled with uncertainty, disaster and fear, where can we find lasting hope? In Luke 8:22–25, Jesus calms a raging storm, revealing his divine authority over creation and his power to save. See why, even when live feels stormy, we can face the future without fear when we trust in the one who promises to rescue us and bring us home to a perfect new creation.

item.title: Judge the Son rightly
item.description: Gwilym Davies - There are so many conflicting voices when it comes to Jesus Christ. It can be overwhelming – and quite discouraging. In John 7, we see that the world can’t think straight about Jesus. But we also see that Jesus has promised to do something about it: to pour out his Spirit like rivers of living water.

item.title: Judge the Son rightly
item.description: Tim Sheppard - When theological experts cast doubt on the teachings of Jesus, it is easy to feel naïve or even to question our beliefs. Have theological experts seen something we haven’t? But John 7 shows us that the crowd has always included so-called ‘expert’ doubters. And just like in Jesus’ day, their doubt does not arise from expertise but rather from poor judgement and ignorance of the Scriptures. Meanwhile, as others in the crowd show us, Jesus really is building his church.

item.title: The Son speaks the words of eternal life
item.description: Gwilym Davies - Sometimes it feels as though everyone is walking away from Jesus. This can be true on a personal level, as old friends quietly drift away from the Christian faith. It can also seem true on a national level, as church congregations gradually decline. But in today's passage, John wants us to see that, however discouraging this may be, it is no reason to stop listening to Jesus. It does not take him by surprise. And Jesus still has the words of eternal life.

item.title: The Son speaks the words of eternal life
item.description: Tim Sheppard - To many, a sermon commending the Bible feels familiar and predictable. However, John 6 concludes with something far more profound, challenging our attitude towards Jesus' words. Peter's famous response to Jesus stands in sharp contrast to that of the other disciples in this passage and provides a crucial model for us to follow.
